topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning outcomes, reviews the historical framework of cancer hallmarks, and frames the lecture's focus on tumor progression mechanisms.

topics.label: Deregulation of growth signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive independent proliferative signaling and bypass growth inhibition.

topics.label: Differentiation block in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells fail to exit the cell cycle and differentiate properly, using examples from hematopoiesis and colonic crypt architecture.

topics.label: Mechanisms of apoptosis resistance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how tumor cells evade programmed cell death through alterations in p53 signaling and the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomeres, and senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit via telomerase reactivation and summarize how p53-mediated stress pathways govern cellular senescence.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire their energy metabolism toward aerobic glycolysis and how metabolic enzyme mutations generate onco-metabolites that alter gene regulation.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the physiological necessity, timing, and molecular balance of new blood vessel formation supporting tumor growth.

topics.label: Metastatic cascade and dissemination
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the multi-step invasion and dissemination process of cancer cells, the seed-and-soil dynamics required for secondary colonization, and the genetic features of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Conclusion and practical session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the discussion of cancer hallmarks, provides concluding advice on the literature, and invites questions before the practicals.
